note: Every entry comes from data/verified-facts/*.json, checked against the official source. Monthly: re-check each source_url, update status, add new programs.

entries.change: The extra bonus of up to $1,000 on BC Hydro heat pump rebates only covers installs completed by October 31, 2026.
entries.instead: If you're replacing electric heat, book your install now to finish before the deadline.

entries.change: HARP helps lower-income households with winter heating bills. It paid $400 last winter and has opened on October 1 in past years. Confirm the 2026-27 date and amount with the Province.
entries.instead: Check your eligibility and apply as soon as the new season opens.

entries.change: Calgary's CEIP financing (up to $50,000 repaid on your property tax) is closed to new applications until winter 2026/2027.
entries.instead: Watch for the reopening, or check whether your town's CEIP is open.

entries.change: Lethbridge's CEIP is at capacity and closed to new pre-qualification. St. Albert is taking waitlist applications only.
entries.instead: Join the waitlist early; it's first come, first served.

entries.program: Federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (Alberta)
entries.change: The federal grant of up to $10,000 to switch from oil to a heat pump closed to Albertans on July 31, 2026.
entries.instead: Income-qualified Calgarians can apply to the Calgary Home Upgrades Program.

entries.change: New rules for invoices from July 6, 2026: heat pump rebates for switching from gas, oil or propane are now $13,000, $7,000 or $3,500 by income level, plus a $3,000 northern top-up for levels 1 and 2.
entries.instead: Check your income level before you get quotes.

entries.program: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (Nova Scotia)
entries.change: Closed to new applicants on July 2, 2026 after funding ran out. A standby list is reviewed only if money frees up.
entries.instead: The Home Energy Assessment still pays up to $5,000, and moderate-income homes can add up to $5,000 more.

entries.change: The provincial top-up was cut from a maximum of $10,000 to $5,000. Stacked with the Home Energy Assessment, the most you can get is now $10,000.
entries.instead: Book a Home Energy Assessment first; it unlocks both.

entries.change: Net metering closed to new customers. New solar owners get the self-generation rate, which pays 10 cents per kWh for power you export.
entries.instead: Size solar for your own use; a battery helps you use more of it yourself.

entries.change: The 30% credit (up to $1,000) for a home EV charger only covers equipment in service by June 30, 2026.
entries.instead: Check your utility for EV charger or panel-upgrade rebates.

entries.change: Con Edison stopped accepting new Level 2 charger applications on April 22, 2026.
entries.instead: Check NYSERDA and your town for other EV charger incentives.

entries.change: The demand-response pilot stopped taking new enrollments on April 9, 2026.
entries.instead: Electrically heated homes can still get a free smart thermostat through Efficiency Nova Scotia.

entries.program: Pasadena Water and Power solar and battery pilot
entries.change: New pilot: $0.60 per watt for rooftop solar ($1.00 for income-qualified homes) and battery incentives up to $550 per kWh. Funds are limited.
entries.instead: Pasadena homeowners should apply early.

entries.change: The income-qualified heat pump rebate (was up to $8,000) was fully reserved statewide on February 24, 2026. New requests are waitlisted.
entries.instead: Income-qualified PG&E and SCE customers can try Energy Savings Assistance for free upgrades.

entries.change: A 0% loan of up to $25,000 for rooftop solar, fully forgiven after 20 years of living in the home.
entries.instead: Boston homeowners: check eligibility with the City.

entries.change: Launched spring 2026: free energy coaching across Waterloo Region, and loans up to $40,000 at 2.5% for GrandBridge Energy customers.
entries.instead: Waterloo Region homeowners can book a free coach.

entries.program: Home Renovation Savings: thermostat and attic
entries.change: The smart thermostat rebate rose to $125 (from $100) and the no-assessment attic insulation rebate to $1,250 (from $1,000).
entries.instead: Claim within 60 days of purchase.

entries.program: Federal home energy tax credits (25C and 25D)
entries.change: The 30% credits for heat pumps, insulation, windows, solar and batteries you own ended for anything installed after December 31, 2025.
entries.instead: Look for state and utility rebates, which still exist in many areas.

entries.change: The last day to submit documents was December 31, 2025. The Greener Homes Loan stopped taking applications October 1, 2025.
entries.instead: Check your province's programs; several still pay for heat pumps and insulation.

entries.program: Efficiency Nova Scotia Home Heating System Rebates
entries.change: Closed December 31, 2025.
entries.instead: Heat pump rebates now come through the Home Energy Assessment.

entries.change: Single-family heat pump and heat pump water heater incentives were fully reserved on November 14, 2025. New requests go on a waitlist.
entries.instead: SMUD customers still have their own heat pump rebates.

entries.change: Closed to homeowners on April 17, 2025.
entries.instead: There's no current solar rebate for Nova Scotia homeowners.

entries.change: Regulators cut the three-year Mass Save budget by $500 million. Residential budgets fell about 25% for gas and 15% for electric.
entries.instead: Heat pump rebates of $2,650 per ton (up to $8,500) are still offered.
